stories.title: Inside the make-or-break AI mega-project behind Nscale's $50b IPO
stories.summary: Nscale's planned $50 billion IPO hinges on the successful execution of a massive AI infrastructure project that would establish the company as a significant compute provider, with investor scrutiny intensifying around construction timelines, power commitments, and customer contracts.
stories.why_it_matters: The IPO's scale tests whether public markets will absorb AI infrastructure risk at valuations previously reserved for hyperscale self-builds, potentially opening or closing a critical funding avenue for dozens of emerging APAC data center developers who lack the balance sheet depth of AWS, Google, or Microsoft to finance multi-gigawatt campuses.
stories.title_zh: Nscale 500亿美元IPO背后的关键AI mega-project内幕
stories.summary_zh: Nscale计划中的500亿美元IPO取决于一个大规模AI基础设施项目的成功执行，该项目将使该公司成为重要的计算提供商，投资者对其建设时间表、电力承诺和客户合同的审查正在加强。
stories.why_zh: 该IPO的规模将测试公开市场是否愿意以先前保留给hyperscale自建项目的估值吸收AI基础设施风险，可能为数十家缺乏AWS、Google或Microsoft资产负债表深度来资助多GW园区的APAC新兴数据中心开发商打开或关闭一条关键融资渠道。
stories.content:
Nscale, one of the UK’s most valuable start-ups, is facing mounting setbacks and financing risks on a vast US data project that underpins its planned $US35 billion ($50 billion) IPO.

The Nvidia-backed “neocloud”, which counts former Meta executive Sheryl Sandberg and ex-UK deputy prime minister Sir Nick Clegg as board members, is pinning its hopes on a rural site in West Virginia to be the main driver of future revenues.

stories.title: An Asian stock trader's guide ahead of the US mid-term elections
stories.summary: Asia’s AI-heavy stock markets face a new US policy wildcard in the mid-term elections, with the outcome potentially reshaping the tech trade and sectors from clean energy to defence.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: 美国中期选举前亚洲股票交易员指南
stories.content:
(Nov 1): Asia’s AI-heavy stock markets face a new US policy wildcard in the mid-term elections, with the outcome potentially reshaping the tech trade and sectors from clean energy to defence.

A Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress would likely bring greater scrutiny of the AI industry and data-centre buildout. An unexpected Republican hold would offer more policy continuity, potentially benefitting Korean and Taiwanese chipmakers and other suppliers to the US technology boom, according to strategists. Currently, polls and prediction markets indicate a high likelihood that Republicans will lose control of the House of Representatives, while the outcome for the Senate is less certain.

Beyond technology, Chinese clean-energy companies could benefit from a stronger Democratic showing, while Japanese defence firms may fare better if Republicans retain control of Congress. A divided government could provide an indirect tailwind for equities by restraining fiscal expansion and putting downward pressure on US bond yields, Lombard Odier noted.

The vote comes at a sensitive time for Asia’s AI trade. Investors are already grappling with elevated borrowing costs, questions over how long the memory-chip boom can last and whether debt-fuelled spending on AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns. The mid-terms add another uncertainty as issues including AI safety, data-centre development and power costs become increasingly politicised in Washington.

“If Dems sweep next week, those issues could become more pressing and those fears could spur another pullback in AI stocks,” said Phillip Wool, head of portfolio management at Rayliant Global Advisors. “Anything that’s a threat to AI is going to weigh heavily on sentiment toward stocks in Korea, Taiwan, Japan, and maybe to a lesser extent, China.”

Still, President Donald Trump retains veto power and broad authority over tariffs, immigration and foreign policy, limiting Democrats’ ability to change his agenda.

Here are the key themes that market participants are watching:

Asia has more at stake in the AI investment boom than most regions, with South Korea and Taiwan supplying many of the advanced semiconductors and other critical hardware underpinning the US data-centre buildout.

That exposure could leave the region vulnerable if a Democratic Congress intensifies scrutiny of the industry. Potential areas of focus include requiring AI developers to shoulder more of the costs of powering data centres and greater congressional oversight of trade and technology policy.

Measures that raise infrastructure and power costs or make data-centre development more difficult could add to investor concerns over the vast sums being spent on AI and the growing debt burden used to finance that expansion.

“Potential changes to the US AI infrastructure build-out, data-centre development or technology restrictions could ultimately reverberate through Asian supply chains” at a time when some money has rotated from AI stocks toward areas such as financials, healthcare and utilities, said Afdhal Rahman, executive director of Wealth Advisory at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp.

Still, investors broadly expect global demand for AI computing power and infrastructure to remain durable regardless of who controls Congress.

Korean and Taiwanese chipmakers remain integral parts of that structural investment, leaving them well placed to weather different election outcomes, Pruksa Lamthongthong, head of Apac equities at Aberdeen Investments, said.

Stocks to watch: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, Samsung Electronics Co, SK Hynix Inc, Hon Hai Precision Industry Co, Quanta Computer Inc, Advantest Corp, Delta Electronics Inc.

The election may also have implications for Chinese stocks, though investors see fewer clear-cut outcomes.

A Democratic sweep and the party’s greater support for clean energy could improve sentiment toward Chinese solar, battery and electric-vehicle companies, according to Rayliant’s Wool. If Democrats take control of Congress, constraints on his domestic agenda could push the administration to rely more heavily on executive powers, leaving trade as one area where the White House retains considerable room to act.

“Tariffs and trade represent the highest-beta channel,” said Wei Li, head of multi-asset investments at BNP Paribas Securities (China), who sees scope for trade tensions to escalate under divided government.

Others expect the mid-terms to have only a limited impact on Chinese equities because the broad direction of US policy toward Beijing enjoys bipartisan support.

China’s more diversified export markets and improving technological capabilities also provide some insulation from shifts in Washington, June Chua, head of Asia equities at Manulife Investment Management, said.

Stocks to watch: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd, BYD Co, Sungrow Power Supply Co, LONGi Green Energy Technology Co, Jinko Solar Co.

For Japanese investors, the election is also being viewed through the lens of geopolitics and oil.

Some, including Kazuyuki Muramatsu, head of investment management at Nagomi Capital, are bracing for a break with the historical pattern of stocks rallying after US mid-term elections. Trump has hinted that US forces could resume strikes on Iran after the vote, raising the risk of another surge in energy prices.

A potential climb in oil toward US$120 a barrel “would overshadow expectations that positive developments could follow the mid-terms,” Muramatsu said.

A Republican hold, meanwhile, could favour Japanese defence companies and US-aligned industrial manufacturers by preserving current spending priorities, according to BNP Paribas’ Li.

The election has the potential to ripple through Asian markets well beyond equities.

The dollar’s recent rally may reverse in the event of a Democratic sweep, increasing signs of a US-Iran compromise and greater scrutiny of AI and data-centre spending, according to Richard Franulovich, Westpac Banking Corp’s head of FX strategy.

Closely contested races that result in recounts or legal challenges could also undermine confidence in US institutions, he said.

Democratic control of Congress will likely curb the scope for further fiscal expansion and ease upward pressure on US interest rates, weighing on the dollar “at the margin,” according to Commonwealth Bank of Australia strategist Carol Kong. A larger-than-expected Republican defeat could prompt a sharper dollar sell-off and make Trump’s policymaking less predictable, potentially boosting the yen as an alternative haven.

Lower US yields and a more constrained fiscal outlook under divided government may benefit Asian exporters and local-currency bonds, BNP Paribas’ Li said.

stories.title: Foxconn explores new OpenAI tie-up for AI hardware
stories.summary: Foxconn chairman Young Liu met with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to explore an expanded partnership beyond their existing data-center rack and AI hardware agreement, potentially encompassing broader co-development of specialized AI infrastructure equipment.
stories.why_it_matters: A deeper Foxconn-OpenAI tie-up would concentrate AI hardware design influence among Taiwanese manufacturing giants, potentially marginalizing traditional server OEMs like Dell and HPE while accelerating the shift toward hyper-customized, vertically optimized rack-scale systems that reduce interoperability and lock customers into specific supply ecosystems.
stories.title_zh: 富士康探索与OpenAI在AI硬件方面的新合作
stories.summary_zh: 富士康董事长刘扬伟与OpenAI CEO Sam Altman会面，探讨在现有数据中心机架和AI硬件协议之外扩大合作，可能涵盖更广泛的专用AI基础设施设备联合开发。
stories.why_zh: 更深层的富士康-OpenAI合作将使AI硬件设计影响力集中于台湾制造业巨头，可能边缘化Dell和HPE等传统服务器OEM，同时加速向超定制化、垂直优化的rack-scale系统转变，这些系统降低互操作性并将客户锁定在特定供应生态系统中。
stories.content:
Foxconn, a major contract electronics manufacturer and Nvidia's largest AI server maker, is exploring a fresh partnership with leading US artificial intelligence developer OpenAI.Foxconn Chairman Young Liu met OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman and indicated a future announcement once details are confirmed, according to a report by Reuters.This potential collaboration would expand on a previous agreement where the two firms worked together on designing and engineering data-centre racks, components, and other AI hardware.Foxconn, formally known as Hon Hai Precision Industry, is increasingly relying on AI infrastructure for its growth. The company expects to maintain double-digit growth next year, dismissing concerns about an AI sector bubble.
### AI Server Manufacturing and Robotics

Foxconn operates six factory buildings in Houston, Texas, where it manufactures AI servers for Nvidia. The company plans further expansion of these facilities.Its cloud and networking products segment, which includes AI servers, accounted for 51 per cent of second-quarter revenue. This marked the first time this segment exceeded 50 per cent of total revenue.Separately, Foxconn is advancing its plans to deploy humanoid robots at its Houston plant. Brand Cheng, chairman of unit Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII), reported that more than 10 humanoid robots are deployed for internal use at its Texas facilities.FII plans to extend this deployment beyond Texas. The unit is also developing AI models for these humanoid robots, based on Nvidia's GR00T foundation model.

stories.title: Nvidia's networking revenue surpasses Cisco's total revenue in Q2
stories.summary: Nvidia's networking business generated over $17.5 billion in second-quarter revenue, surpassing Cisco's entire company revenue of $17.3 billion for the same quarter, underscoring how AI-driven datacenter interconnect demand has eclipsed traditional enterprise networking.
stories.why_it_matters: The revenue crossover marks a structural power shift in enterprise infrastructure procurement, where AI workload requirements now dictate networking architecture decisions—forcing Cisco and legacy vendors to accelerate their own AI fabric strategies or risk permanent displacement from the most lucrative segments of the datacenter buildout.
stories.title_zh: Nvidia网络业务Q2收入超越Cisco总收入
stories.summary_zh: Nvidia的networking业务在第二季度创造超过175亿美元收入，超过同期Cisco全公司173亿美元的总收入，凸显了AI驱动的datacenter interconnect需求如何超越传统企业网络市场。
stories.why_zh: 这一收入交叉标志着企业基础设施采购中的结构性权力转移，AI工作负载需求现在决定networking架构决策——迫使Cisco和传统供应商加速自身的AI fabric战略，否则将面临从数据中心建设中最有利可图的领域被永久取代的风险。
stories.content:
Nvidia's networking revenues reached over $17.5 billion in Q2, surpassing Cisco's total revenue of $17.3 billion during the same period. The company's emergence as a networking power follows its 2019 acquisition of Mellanox for $6.9 billion.At the time of acquisition, Mellanox was known for its ConnectX NICs and InfiniBand switches, primarily used in high-performance computing (HPC) and supercomputing clusters. Nvidia repositioned itself as a system builder, integrating compute and networking for distributed AI workloads, according to Dell'Oro Group analyst Sameh Boujelbene.Boujelbene noted that customers select Nvidia for its tightly integrated compute and networking architecture, optimised for AI workloads. This integration simplifies deployments and accelerates time to market. Ben Mabey, CTO of Recursion, an AI and machine learning company, stated that Nvidia's integration schemes simplified optimisation and troubleshooting for their large datasets.Nvidia's networking revenues surged after the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT in 2023 and with the rollout of Blackwell-generation GPUs in 2024 and 2025. Boujelbene identified two major inflection points: the introduction of NVLink switches and the accelerating adoption of Spectrum-X Ethernet switches for AI back-end networks.NVSwitch now accounts for approximately one-third of Nvidias networking revenue, up from nearly zero less than two years ago, Boujelbene told The Register. Nvidia is further expanding its networking business by licensing its NVLink Fusion interconnect technology to third parties like Marvell, Qualcomm, and Arm. This move extends Nvidia's networking footprint beyond its own GPUs into the custom accelerator market.

- AI & Compute Infrastructure
- 1 min Read

# Nvidia's networking revenue surpasses Cisco's total revenue in Q2

Nvidia's networking division reported revenues topping $17.5 billion in Q2, exceeding Cisco's total revenue of $17.3 billion for the same period. This growth highlights Nvidia's strategic shift into datacenter networking for AI workloads.

- Published On Nov 01, 2026 at 07:40 AM IST

## Highlights

- Nvidia's Q2 networking revenue hit $17.5 billion, exceeding Cisco's total revenue of $17.3 billion.
- The company's networking growth stems from its 2019 Mellanox acquisition for $6.9 billion.
- Nvidia integrates compute and networking architectures for optimised AI workload performance.
- NVSwitch contributes roughly one-third of Nvidia's networking revenue, up from near zero.
- Nvidia licenses NVLink Fusion to partners like Marvell and Arm, expanding its networking reach.

stories.title: OpenAI's Altman meets Samsung executives as chip crunch deepens
stories.summary: Sam Altman held discussions with Samsung's leadership in Seoul on Saturday, focusing on strengthening collaboration around memory chip supply and AI infrastructure development as worldwide shortages of critical components worsen.
stories.why_it_matters: Samsung's dominance in HBM memory gives OpenAI leverage against Nvidia's integrated supply chain, while the meeting signals that AI labs are bypassing traditional semiconductor distributors to secure direct allocations—accelerating vertical integration trends that threaten standalone chip vendors and colocation providers alike.

stories.title_zh: 芯片短缺加剧之际，OpenAI Altman会见Samsung高管
stories.summary_zh: Sam Altman于周六在首尔与三星集团高层举行会谈，聚焦于加强memory chip供应和AI基础设施开发方面的合作，因为全球关键组件短缺状况正在恶化。
stories.why_zh: 三星在HBM memory领域的主导地位使OpenAI在与Nvidia集成供应链的博弈中获得杠杆，同时此次会议表明AI实验室正在绕过传统半导体分销商以确保直接分配——加速垂直整合趋势，这对独立芯片供应商和colocation提供商都构成威胁。
stories.content:
(Oct 31): OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman met with Samsung Group’s top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure as global shortages intensify.

Samsung hosted Altman for talks with about 50 executives from its electronics, financial and biotechnology affiliates in Yongin, south of Seoul, the South Korean company said in a statement. The discussions focused on how AI can reshape industries, corporate decision-making and business opportunities over the next decade.

The meeting comes as shortages in a broad array of memory products strain the global electronics industry and send chip prices soaring. Demand from data-centre operators is intensifying competition for supplies, with the five biggest players in the AI infrastructure race planning to spend more than US$3 trillion (RM12.17 trillion) in the coming years. Memory accounts for roughly a third of data-centre spending.

Altman is the latest American tech leader to visit South Korea, the leader in advanced memory chips and a country where AI adoption is accelerating among businesses and consumers. Nvidia Corp CEO Jensen Huang and Advanced Micro Devices Inc's Lisa Su both visited twice since last year to strengthen supply-chain ties. Technology executives have warned that chip production is struggling to keep pace with demand.

Saturday’s meeting builds on a partnership announced earlier to supply memory chips for OpenAI’s Stargate infrastructure project and cooperate on AI data centres, including floating offshore facilities. Samsung is also accelerating AI adoption across its businesses, from research and manufacturing to marketing and corporate operations.
